target: Route "gadget": Realising the second blow-up level by hand (labels gad:), audited for CORRECTNESS

findings.defect: GAP: the "in particular" clause of gad:B2-rows -- no Max vertex of a B^2 realisation may have an action that goes straight to the sinks, nor one that returns only to itself and the sinks -- does NOT follow from gad:mono as stated, because gad:mono assumes BOTH p-hat^{i,1} >= p-hat^{i,0} AND q-hat^{i,1} >= q-hat^{i,0}, so its contrapositive only yields that the PAIRS (p-hat,q-hat) are incomparable, which a pure self-return survives. The missing statement, in one sentence: IF p-hat^{i,1} >= p-hat^{i,0} COMPONENTWISE OFF i, WITH NO HYPOTHESIS ON q-hat, THEN {g_i=+} IS UP-CLOSED FOR THE REACHABILITY PREORDER (dually for <=). The repair is free: the given proof of gad:mono uses only the coefficient vector p-hat^{i,1}-p-hat^{i,0}, a constant shift being irrelevant to monotonicity in y; with the strengthened lemma the p-hat rows alone must be incomparable at every Max vertex of a B^2 realisation, p-hat^{i,0}=0 is then excluded, and the clause is true.
findings.evidence: The route's own H (gad:xor, 100-vertex realisation of B(2-cube)) is the counterexample to the deduction: at x_1, action 0 is a pure self-return, p-hat^{1,0}=(0,0,0) and q-hat^{1,0}=21/172, p-hat^{1,1}>=0 and q-hat^{1,1}=0, so the (p-hat,q-hat) pairs ARE incomparable while the p-hat vectors are comparable (rows.py: 'x1: (p,q) incomparable:True ; p-hat incomparable:False ; p-hat^0 = [0,0,0]'). I verified the repaired chain: for B^2 all five coordinates have {g=+} neither up- nor down-closed (mono.py), and the delivered 138-vertex normal form has all six controlled vertices p-hat-incomparable (rows.py). The claimed witness edges of gad:B2-rows all check out exactly (x: 0->4, 8->0; a1: 0->1, 8->0; b1: 2->3, 3->1; a2: 17->16, 18->19; b2: 8->0, 9->8), as does the B^1 claim that only beta_1 needs incomparable rows ({g=+} down-closed at x and at alpha_1).

findings.defect: The stated verification "val_sigma increases at every one of the 136 non-sink vertices at every round of the run" (repeated in the route's LaTeX proof as "as lem:switch requires") is false, and it also misstates lem:switch, which requires strict increase only on the switched set S and non-decrease elsewhere. The theorem itself is unaffected.
findings.evidence: Recomputed all 11 value vectors of the run 12->19->13->17->8->16->0->7->1->5->4 on the built game (strict.py): non-strict rounds are round 0-3 (3 of 136 vertices unchanged), rounds 4 and 5 (83 of 136 unchanged, e.g. vertices 0,1,2,5,6,7,8,9), rounds 6 and 9 (31 unchanged), rounds 7 and 8 (66 unchanged). What does hold, and I verified it, is: nondecreasing at all 136 non-sinks at every round, strictly increasing somewhere at every round. (The root agent's integrated prop:b2-realised already softened this to "the value vector increases at every step".)

findings.defect: "gad:precision-blowup shows d_k >= k+1" conflates the number of average vertices with the dyadic denominator EXPONENT d of the normal form. gad:precision bounds |Vavg| >= log_2(h-1); it places no lower bound whatever on d, since the only stated link is a <= O(|C|^2 d), which inverts to d >= Omega(k/|C|^2) -- vacuous once |C| grows. The proved statement is a_k >= k+1, which supports "the first size statement about the tower" but not "the precision must grow additively".
findings.evidence: gad:precision-blowup's own conclusion reads "at least log_2(h(s)-1) AVERAGE VERTICES"; the realisation bound quoted in the same remark is |Vavg| = O(|C|^2 d), an UPPER bound on a, so a >= k+1 constrains |C|^2 d from below and d not at all. Numerically: level 1 has a=53 with d=6, level 2 has a=130 with d=9, against required a >= log2(3)=1.58 and log2(9)=3.17 respectively -- the bound is nowhere near binding on either quantity.

findings.defect: Arithmetic slip in the conditional size estimate: with |C_k| = 3k and d_k = 3k+3 the remark's own realisation bound O(|C|^2 d) gives N = O(k^3) = O(m^3), not the claimed "N = O(k^2) = O(m^2)". The route's results list contradicts itself on the same line ("N = O(m^2) if the increments persist, N = O(m^3) in general"). The conclusion -- polynomial size, so prop:auso-size's size clause is met and all-switches is superpolynomial -- survives either way, since 3*2^k-2 = 2^{Omega(N^{1/3})}.
findings.evidence: O(|C|^2 d) with |C|=3k, d=3k+3 is 9k^2 * (3k+3) = Theta(k^3). Checked against the two data points (|C|=3,d=6 -> bound 54, actual a=53; |C|=6,d=9 -> bound 324, actual a=130).

findings.defect: The one-line justification of part (c) -- "a square whose two coordinates both have a non-constant g is the directed 4-cycle, which has two sinks" -- is wrong twice: such a square need not be a 4-cycle, and a directed 4-cycle has NO sink, not two. The conclusion of (c) is nevertheless correct.
findings.evidence: Exhaustive enumeration of the 16 genuine orientations of the square (square.py): exactly 4 have both coordinates non-constant; 2 of them are directed 4-cycles (0 sinks, 0 sources) and 2 have 2 sinks and 2 sources; none satisfies the Szabo-Welzl condition. The rest of gad:face reconstructs correctly: (a) the |C|-2 shared rows are a subset of the rows of the invertible I-M of each corner's system, hence independent, so Pi has dimension exactly 2; (b)'s parallel-lines and sign-change arguments are valid, and all four value vectors of a face are distinct because val_sigma = val_sigma' would force Delta_i = 0 against nondegeneracy.

findings.defect: The "Hence sign Delta_0 = NOT(sigma_1 XOR L)" of part (iii) does not follow from the displayed inequalities max_{L=0}T < 21/172 < min_{L=1}T. Those settle only the eight strategies with sigma_1 = 0, where z_1 is pinned to 21/172; for the eight with sigma_1 = 1 the comparison z_1 vs T is left undetermined by the display and requires eight further exact comparisons. The claimed pattern is nonetheless TRUE.
findings.evidence: I performed the eight missing comparisons exactly (xor.py): at k=2,3,6,7,10,11 (L=0, sigma_1=1) z_1 < T, e.g. k=2 gives z_1 = 2154587/34494818 < T = 2651327/34494818; at k=14,15 (L=1) z_1 > T. All of gad:xor's numbers reproduce exactly: val(x_1)=21/172 whenever sigma_1=0; 256*Delta_1 = 7z_0-71z_1+133z_2+102z_3-21 with sign string '------------++++' = L; 256*Delta_0 = 165z_1+4z_3-40z_0-121z_2-2 with sign string '++--++--++----++' = NOT(sigma_1 XOR L); max_{L=0}T = 2497696403/23623057920 and min_{L=1}T = 347482169/2787045602 exactly as stated; and the claimed isomorphism (seed (3,2,0,1), u with z = e_1, permutation (0,1,3,2) plus complementation) maps H's outmap onto B(2-cube) exactly (iso.py).

findings.defect: "The prescribed response used is tau = 1 exactly when the first two Max coordinates are both 1" is not a property of the delivered game: its actual Min best response at c_6 is tau = 1 exactly at sigma in {11,15,19,23,27,31}, and at sigma = 3 and sigma = 7 (where the prescription says 1) the best response is strictly tau = 0. Since the remark says the prescription's optimality was "imposed as explicit constraints", the recipe as printed will not reproduce the game. Bears on the reproducibility instructions in "next steps", not on any theorem.
findings.evidence: tau.py, exact: best-response string over sigma = 0..31 is 00000000000100010001000100010001, against the prescription 00010001000100010001000100010001; strict (untied) preference at every sigma. The three critical 2-faces named in gad:B2-min do carry a varying response ([0,0,0,1] on each of {8,9,10,11}, {16,17,18,19}, {24,25,26,27}) and the non-critical fourth face {0,1,2,3} carries a constant one, exactly as gad:B2-min requires.

findings.defect: The closing sentence "The orientation is not Holt-Klee, so by prop:oneplayer-lp the Min vertex is necessary" drops the nondegeneracy hypothesis that prop:oneplayer-lp carries; rem:oneplayer-lp states explicitly that DEGENERATE one-player games are not bound by Holt-Klee, so the correct claim is that no NONDEGENERATE one-player realisation exists. gad:B2-min states the qualifier correctly.
findings.evidence: prop:oneplayer-lp (frontier.tex line 4264) begins "Let G be a nondegenerate stopping SSG with Vmin = emptyset"; rem:blowup-measured itself says "any realisation needs Min vertices OR TIES".

findings.defect: The remark asserts as a general fact that the forbidden-pair test "is implied by, but strictly weaker than, Holt-Klee". The implication is verified only at m = 4; no proof is offered and none is obvious. (Both are proved necessary conditions for nondegenerate one-player realisability -- Holt-Klee by prop:oneplayer-lp, no-forbidden-pair by gad:B2-min -- but neither is known to imply the other in general.)
findings.evidence: My independent census (census4.c, from scratch: 5541744 USOs, 4792176 AUSOs, 12640 classes, matching prop:auso-census) gives HK classes 6113, classes with a forbidden pair 4365, HK-and-forbidden 0, non-HK-and-forbidden 4365, non-HK-and-no-forbidden 2162 -- every one of the route's census numbers, at m=4 only.

findings.defect: "a shrinking fraction, but exponentially many, so the Min response map must be active across a constant fraction of the cube" -- a shrinking fraction is precisely what rules out the stated conclusion. The measurement shows the forbidden pairs grow by about 4.4x per level while the two-faces grow by about 6.5x, i.e. active on exponentially many but a vanishing fraction of faces.
findings.evidence: Recomputed the whole table (forbrun.py): forbidden pairs 0,4,28,136,600 at levels 1..5 out of 6,80,672,4608,28160 two-faces -- exactly the route's numbers; ratios 4/80=0.050, 28/672=0.042, 136/4608=0.030, 600/28160=0.021.

verdict:
SOUND. Nothing fatal or major survives. I rebuilt every computational claim from the STATEMENTS, in exact rational arithmetic, in /tmp/claude-1000/-data-ssg-proof/6e64b33d-520c-4c82-aa1b-ffb69ecfcb61/scratchpad/audit-gadget-correctness/, with my own cores (cube.py, nf.py, gamecore.py, hk.py, forb.py, census4.c).

WHAT REPRODUCED EXACTLY.
(1) gad:B2, the headline. Building B^2 = B(B(1-cube)) from thm:blowup's own definition (1-cube seeded with sink 1, then u = 4, z = e_{beta_1}) gives the outmap (7,4,5,2,0,1,3,6,24,9,27,14,31,28,29,10,16,25,19,30,23,20,21,26,8,17,11,22,15,12,13,18) -- identical to the claim, USO, acyclic, heights exactly as printed, max 10, walk from 12 = 12,19,13,17,8,16,0,7,1,5,4 with exactly the ten printed switched sets. Typing the twelve rows from the theorem's statement and evaluating val_sigma as the componentwise MINIMUM over both positional Min strategies of the exact pair values (never policy iteration), checking each is a fixed point of T_sigma, reproduces that outmap with zero ties among the 160 incidences. Independently, B2_small_GAME.json: 138 vertices (5 Max, 1 Min, 130 avg, 2 sinks), every non-sink of out-degree 2, GREATEST TRAP EMPTY so stopping by lem:trapchar, 64 pair values by my own elimination, outmap from the game's own successors (own-successor test, not the pair test) = B^2, nondegenerate, Szabo-Welzl on all C(32,2) pairs, acyclic, Holt-Klee FAILS (8 violating 3-faces, unit vertex-capacity max-flow), and the harmonic normal form recovered from the game equals the printed rows at denominator 512. All ELEVEN rows of gad:B2-run's exact value table match to the last fraction, and val_sigma(4) is the componentwise maximum over all 32 strategies. The second realisation (155 vertices, denominator 2^10) also realises B^2, and B1_game.json (58 vertices, 3 Max, 0 Min, 53 avg, denominator 2^6) realises B^1 of height 4. This settles the instance rem:blowup-measured called the smallest open one, and it is a genuine result.
(2) gad:B2-min. The four forbidden pairs are exactly as described (face {x,alpha_1} at beta_1=0; alpha_2 at layers (0,1),(1,1); beta_2 at layers (1,0),(1,1)), the tower counts 0,4,28,136,600 out of 6,80,672,4608,28160 are exact, and the delivered game's Min best response varies on precisely the three critical faces and is constant on the fourth.
(3) The census. A from-scratch C enumeration reproduces 5541744 USOs, 4792176 AUSOs, 12640 classes, the height histogram 1:1 2:754 3:4776 4:5404 5:1561 6:143 7:1, 6113 Holt-Klee classes, 4365 classes with a forbidden pair, ZERO of them Holt-Klee, 2162 non-HK without -- every number the route reports, and the height-7 class does carry a forbidden pair.
(4) gad:xor. Every quantity, including both exact threshold bounds.
(5) gad:face(b). Tested EXACTLY (the route tested numerically) on all three realisations: 12 + 48 = 60 (face,coordinate) tests on the one-player games with 0 mismatches, and 96 tests on the two-player game (32 faces correctly skipped because the Min response varies) with 0 mismatches once the nine parallel-segment cases are resolved -- all nine have g_c constant and disjoint parallel segments, as the lemma predicts.
(6) gad:pi. The proof is sound, and on the published 58-vertex realisation the Radon certificate exists exactly, supported precisely on the four beta_1 = 0 strategies, with the crossing point strictly interior to both segments.
(7) gad:readout and gad:precision. Both reconstruct line by line. gad:readout's prefactors (1-p^{i,1}_i) and (1-p^{i,0}_i) are right. gad:precision's telescoping is right (2*sum_{t=1}^{h-1}|Delta_t| <= sum_t |w|.d_t = |w|.(z_h-z_0) <= ||w||_1 <= 2), lem:switch gives d_t >= 0, lem:denominator-sharp with r = |Vavg| gives one common denominator D <= 2^a for val_sigma (val_sigma is the value of the sub-SSG with Max frozen, same average part), and the alternating sequence in cor:precision-blowup is legitimate: switching only the inner part s(v_t) at layer (alpha,beta) = (0,1) keeps a nonempty subset of the strictly switchable set, and g_alpha = + iff (beta = 1 and h(v) odd) so the incidence alternates. The tower heights are 3*2^k-2 = 4,10,22,46,94 as claimed.

STANDING ERRORS: none found. val_sigma is never computed by greedy policy iteration; rows are accumulated, not dict literals; the trap admits t0; the own-successor test is used throughout; the terminal round is not counted (10 productive rounds, sink at 4); no unreachable-vertex separation; no oracle that is target-equivalent is assumed anywhere (the route claims no decision rule, no barrier and no algorithm -- it is a construction plus four necessary conditions).

THE ONE REAL GAP, restated for the record: gad:B2-rows's "in particular no Max vertex may have an action that goes straight to the sinks, nor one that returns only to itself and the sinks" is not implied by gad:mono as stated, and the route's own H is a game where incomparable (p-hat,q-hat) pairs coexist with a pure self-return. The missing sentence is: "If p-hat^{i,1} >= p-hat^{i,0} componentwise off i, with no hypothesis on q-hat, then {g_i = +} is up-closed for the reachability preorder." That sentence is proved by the argument already printed for gad:mono, so the repair is one word ("under the stated inequality on p-hat") and the clause is then true -- I verified the repaired chain end to end.

The route's gap statement and hedging are honest: the additive-precision question is correctly left open, "two data points do not make a recurrence" is stated, and neither denominator is claimed least.
